# S134 - AI in decisions: provider SPI, AI skills and the AI task step, evaluation and shadow mode, decision records, long-running AI tasks

Wave B of [doc 29](../29-camunda-gap-implementation-plan.md) section 7: CG-A04, CG-A01 (with the section 7.4 guardrail pipeline, 7.5 calibration and 7.6 autonomy policy), CG-A02, CG-A03 and CG-A05. CG-A06 (document extraction) and CG-A07 (operator explain) were not started.

Decisions applied (from the coordinating session): D-CG3, autonomy default `suggest`, `auto` only for labels the workspace policy marks low-risk, adverse outcomes in regulated workspaces always need a person; D-CG9, decision-record input retention default `digest`. Elsewhere the doc's recommended defaults were taken.

Flyway: V260 only (V261-V269 unused). OpenAPI: one paths block and one schemas block, both comment-delimited "AiSkills", tag `AiSkills` after `AI`. Compiler version not bumped: AI task BPMN is generated only when a workflow has an `aiTask` step, so no golden file moves.

## 1. Model provider SPI (CG-A04)

- `com.orqix.ai.provider.ModelProvider`: `kind()` and `complete(endpoint, credential, ModelRequest)` returning `ModelResponse` (content, model used, finish reason, input/output/cached tokens, cost, whether the schema was enforced, mean token probability). Failures are the existing `ProviderException` kinds (classified by HTTP status, never carrying bodies).
- Adapters (JDK `HttpClient`, no SDKs, redirects never followed, 4 MiB answer limit):
  - `OpenAiCompatibleProvider`: `POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions` (OpenRouter, vLLM, Ollama `/v1`, LM Studio); bearer key optional (private endpoints); `response_format.json_schema` with `strict: true`; optional `logprobs`. The OpenRouter endpoint keeps the S10 extras (`provider.max_price`, usage accounting, `X-Title`).
  - `AnthropicProvider`: `POST /v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`; fixed instructions as a system block with `cache_control` (prompt caching); strict output with `output_config.format` (`json_schema`); no sampling settings (this API version refuses them); a `refusal` stop reason is a refused request.
  - `BedrockProvider`: Converse `POST /model/{modelId}/converse`; IAM keys from a JSON secret signed with Signature V4 (service `bedrock`, path segments encoded twice, session token supported) or a Bedrock API key as bearer; strict output as a forced `answer` tool whose input schema is the answer schema.
  - `AzureOpenAiProvider`: `/openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions?api-version=...` (default `2024-10-21`), `api-key` header or an Entra bearer token; model-to-deployment map.
  - `VertexGeminiProvider`: `generateContent`; Vertex (`{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/{m}`) with a bearer token when `project` is set, else the Gemini API with `x-goog-api-key`; strict output with `responseMimeType: application/json` and `responseJsonSchema`.
- `ProviderRegistry` is the entry point other AI features use (the agent-tools session can move `ToolChat` onto it; `ToolChat`, `AgentExecutor`, `McpClient` and agent connections are untouched here). `resolve(profileId, allowedResidency)` applies the existing policy: S10 profiles (`orqix.ai.profiles`) go through `ModelPolicy` unchanged (catalog, excluded globs, allowlist, price caps, circuit breaker); profiles declared under `orqix.ai.model-providers.profiles` name an endpoint and declare their prices, checked against the same excluded globs, allowlist and price caps. A residency rule admits only endpoints carrying one of its tags. `complete(...)` resolves the credential and fills the cost from declared prices when the provider reports none.
- Configuration (`ProviderProperties`, prefix `orqix.ai.model-providers`): `endpoints.<id>.{kind, base-url, secret-ref, region, project, location, api-version, deployments, residency[], strict-schema, logprobs, timeout}`, `profiles.<id>.{provider, model, label, input-per-million, output-per-million}`, `open-router-residency[]` (default none: OpenRouter routing is not bound to a region, so it fails every residency rule).
- Credentials: `com.orqix.integration.ModelProviderSecrets` resolves `secret-ref` through the S132 `SecretResolver` (file, Vault, AWS, Azure, Google), counted in the secret-access audit; `webhook-` references are refused. The AI module never reads `SecretStore` (ArchitectureTest rule kept).

## 2. AI skills (CG-A01)

- Contract `contracts/ai-skill-v1.schema.json` (packaged with the compiler like the connection schemas), two kinds: `skill` (key, name, mode, instructions, typed `input` with `classification`, mode members `labels` with `risk` and `adverse` / `fields` / `score` / `outcomes` / `summary`, approved `examples`, `modelProfile`, `confidence` (`single` or `selfConsistency` with 1-5 samples), `evaluation` (suite, `minAccuracy`, `minRecall` per label, `minCases` default 50), `limits` (tokens, `maxCostUsd`, `timeoutSeconds` up to 600), `promotion` (`minShadowCases` default 200, `targetAgreement` default 0.9), `drift` (`maxAgreementDrop` default 0.1, `fallbackToSuggest` default true)) and `evaluationSuite` (cases with input, expected label/fields/score+tolerance/outcome/mustMention and source).
- `com.orqix.compiler.AiSkillContracts` (pure Java): schema plus semantic checks (duplicates, members that do not fit the mode, score range, recall targets on unknown labels, samples need selfConsistency), suite checks against a skill, the JCS content hash, and the compile facts of a version. Registration and the compiler read a skill the same way.
- Lifecycle (`AiSkills`): a designer (`workflow.edit`) creates a skill (version 1, draft), changes a draft, submits it (the profile must resolve) and adds new versions (one in progress at a time). A different person holding the new grant-only `ai.approve-skill` approves a submitted version with a reason (fresh access; author refused with 403 `SELF_APPROVAL_DENIED`; CHECK constraint `approver_id <> author_id`). Approved versions never change; earlier approved versions stay approved for the releases that pinned them; retiring a version is the kill switch (its AI tasks go to `aiUnavailable`). New problem code `AI_SKILL_STATE_CONFLICT` (409).
- Grants: `ai.approve-skill` and `ai.evaluate`, workspace-wide, no role carries them (V260 widens the two `permission_grant` checks; `AccessService`, `AccessController`, OpenAPI enums, Settings help text).

## 3. The AI task step (CG-A01)

- Schema (`workflow-v0.schema.json`): node `aiTask` with `config.{skillRef, skillVersion?, mode, inputMapping, autonomy (shadow|suggest|autoWithReview|auto, default suggest), minConfidence (default 0.8), reviewSamplePercent (default 10), redaction (per input: maskCardNumbersAndEmails, maskDigits, hash, drop)}`; transition `on` gains `aiLabel` (with the new member `aiLabel`), `lowConfidence`, `needsReview`, `aiUnavailable`.
- Compile context: `CompileContext.aiSkills` (`AiSkillInfo` / `AiSkillVersion` / `AiLabel`), filled by `CompileContextFactory` through `AiTaskPort.skillFacts` (approval, contract facts, autonomy ceiling, the passing evaluation run within 30 days on the version's profile).
- Rules (`AiTaskRules`, wired into `GraphRules` for the allowed routes):
  - `WF_AI_SKILL_UNKNOWN`, `WF_AI_SKILL_NOT_APPROVED` (no approved version, or the step's pin is not approved), `WF_AI_SKILL_MODE`.
  - Publish gate `WF_AI_EVALUATION_REQUIRED`: a passing evaluation run on the pinned profile within 30 days; shadow mode is exempt so evidence can be collected first.
  - `WF_AI_AUTONOMY_NOT_PROMOTED` (autonomy above the version's ceiling), `WF_AI_AUTONOMY_MODE` (score, recommend and summarize allow only shadow or suggest), warnings `WF_AI_AUTO_NO_LOW_RISK`, `WF_AI_REVIEW_SAMPLE_UNUSED`, `WF_AI_THRESHOLD_UNUSED`, `WF_AI_SUGGEST_ALWAYS_REVIEWS`, `WF_AI_RECOMMEND_TARGET`.
  - Inputs: `WF_AI_INPUT_MISSING`, `WF_AI_INPUT_UNKNOWN`, `WF_AI_INPUT_TYPE`, `WF_AI_INPUT_OPTIONAL`, `WF_AI_REDACTION_UNKNOWN`, plus the usual availability checks.
  - Routes `WF_AI_ROUTES`, `WF_AI_LABEL_ROUTE`, `WF_AI_LABEL_UNKNOWN`, `WF_AI_LABEL_ROUTE_SUGGEST`: classify has one path per label (when it routes), `lowConfidence`, an optional `needsReview` and `aiUnavailable`; extract has `next`, `needsReview`, `aiUnavailable`; score, recommend, summarize have `next` and `aiUnavailable`; shadow has `next` only.
- Outputs (`/steps/<id>/`): `status` (decided, lowConfidence, needsReview, unavailable, shadow) and `skillVersion` always; `confidence`, `modelUsed` and the mode's values (`label`+`reasons`, extracted fields, `score`+`reasons`, `recommendation`+`rationale`, `summary`) only when AI answered: a reference reachable through `aiUnavailable` is `WF_FIELDREF_NOT_GUARANTEED`. Shadow answers are marked as possibly missing, so they can never change the request.
- BPMN: an async, triggerable service task `${orqixAiTask}` with `orqix:aiTask` (skill, pinned `skillVersion`, `contentHash`, mode, autonomy, threshold, sample, `orqix:input`, `orqix:redaction`, `pinnedByDesigner` when the step pins) and a generated exclusive gateway `<id>__aiRoute` whose flows test `${orqixRoute.ai(execution, '<id>', '<route>')}` (`label:<key>` for labels). Shadow tasks have no gateway (one path). The BPMN reader reads it back (round trip exact; the publish pin is dropped unless the designer pinned). `CompiledWorkflow.aiSkills` and the release manifest `aiSkills` record the pin and the evaluation run.
- Simulator and Test tab: `ai.<stepId>` in the scenario (`label`, `confidence`, `fields`, `score`, `recommendation`, `summary`, `unavailable`); no model is called; the route follows the runtime rules (shadow continues, suggest goes to a person, below threshold takes lowConfidence or needsReview). Workspace policy downgrades are applied by the runtime only.

## 4. Guardrail pipeline (section 7.4) - `AiTaskEngine`

1. Admission: the pinned version is still approved and its hash matches the release; inputs fit their declared length; the profile resolves under the workspace residency rule; outside shadow mode, a passing evaluation run on the profile within 30 days; budget left (monthly budget, per-request maximum, the skill's `maxCostUsd`, default 0.05). Effective autonomy: the step's, capped by the version's promotion ceiling, `suggest` after a drift fallback, `suggest` when the policy disallows `autoWithReview`.
2. Minimization: only mapped values; each value gets the stricter of its classification action (policy defaults: public/internal send, customer-text mask, personal hash, sensitive drop) and the step's redaction rule. Masking replaces card numbers and e-mail addresses.
3. Prompt: pinned instructions, labels/fields/outcomes, approved examples and an output contract as the system text (identical per version, cacheable); request values as JSON inside `<request_data>` and declared to be data, never instructions.
4. Provider call through the SPI with the task deadline (skill `timeoutSeconds`, at most 10 minutes) and the cost ceiling.
5. Validation against the mode's answer schema (labels from the enum, typed fields, score range, summary length); one repair turn per sample, then the sample is invalid.
6. Consistency: `selfConsistency` takes N samples (temperature 0 then 0.7 where allowed) and the majority; agreement is the share of valid samples that agree.
7. Calibration (section 7.5): the raw score comes from checkable signals (agreement across samples, else mean token probability when returned, else the model's own figure; extraction takes the lowest field confidence; a repair lowers it by 10 %); it is then mapped to the observed accuracy of its bucket in the version's latest passing evaluation run (buckets with 5 or more cases).
8. Routing (section 7.6): shadow always continues; below threshold takes `lowConfidence` (classify) or `needsReview` (extract); `suggest` goes to a person (`needsReview` when the step has it, else `lowConfidence`); in a regulated workspace an `adverse` label always goes to a person; `auto` decides only labels listed as `skillKey:label` in the policy's low-risk list; `autoWithReview` decides and marks a deterministic sample (`reviewSamplePercent`) for review. Anything that fails ends on `aiUnavailable` (shadow: `next`).
9. Record: the decision record is written in the transaction that completes the step (section 6).

Metering: one `ai_generation` row per task (`kind aiTask`) and per evaluation run (`kind aiEval`), so the monthly budget stays one number.

## 5. Long-running AI tasks (CG-A05)

- `AiTaskDelegate` (`orqixAiTask`) resolves the mapped values and queues an `ai_task_job` row in the job transaction with the input sealed (AES-256-GCM, job id and purpose as associated data); the step shows as current step kind `ai`; event `AI_TASK_QUEUED`.
- `AiTaskWorker` (runtime) claims jobs (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, lease `orqix.ai.tasks.lease-seconds` default 60, fence), runs the pipeline outside any transaction on virtual threads (`threads` default 4) and renews the lease between turns, so a task may run until its deadline (hard cap 10 minutes after queueing, `max-timeout`). Completion (`AiTaskJobs.complete`): decision record, step outputs and route variable, step removal, `AI_TASK_COMPLETED` and the engine trigger in one transaction; a busy engine is retried, else the lease expires and the job is retried.
- Turn state (`TurnVault`, `ai_turn_state`): every completed sample (validated answer, repair flag, usage) is sealed after each call; a job reclaimed after a crash continues from the last completed turn and repeats no provider call. Turn state and the sealed input are deleted when the step ends (completion, cancellation by the engine via the delegate's `ACTIVITY_CANCELLED` listener) and swept at most 24 hours after they were written. The key is the S132 secret `orqix.ai.tasks.turn-state-key-ref` (default `ai-turn-state-key`, 32 bytes Base64); without it a random per-pod key is used and logged once (a crash then restarts the task from its first turn).
- Recovery every 15 s: an expired lease returns the job to the queue; after `max-attempts` (default 3) or past the deadline the job ends on `aiUnavailable` with a record that says why. `orqix.ai.tasks.worker-enabled=false` keeps a pod from running AI tasks.

## 6. Evaluation, shadow mode and feedback (CG-A02)

- Suites (`ai_eval_suite`, `PUT /ai-eval-suites/{key}`, `workflow.edit`): synthetic or deliberately redacted cases; nothing copies production data in.
- Runs (`POST /ai-skills/{key}/versions/{v}/evaluations`, `ai.evaluate`, 202, background): every case through the same inference path as production (minimization, samples, repair) on the version's profile. Metrics: accuracy, per-label precision/recall/support, confusion matrix, invalid answers, total cost and cost per case, p95 latency, ten calibration buckets and the threshold trade-off (share decided automatically and its observed accuracy at 0.5-0.95). Pass: at least `minCases`, accuracy at least `minAccuracy` (default 0.9) and every `minRecall`. The release evidence pack lists each AI task with its pinned version, profile, autonomy and the evaluation run that passed the gate.
- Shadow dashboard (`GET .../shadow`): decisions, shadow decisions, compared (with a human outcome), agreement, statuses, confusion (AI value to human value), per-label precision/recall, cost per case, p95 latency, promotion thresholds, ceiling and drift state.
- Promotion (`POST .../promotions`, `workflow.edit`; `POST /ai-skill-promotions/{id}/decision`, `ai.approve-skill`, four eyes): one step at a time (`suggest -> autoWithReview -> auto`), only with at least `minShadowCases` compared cases and agreement at or above `targetAgreement`; the evidence is stored with the request; approval raises `autonomy_ceiling`.
- Drift (weekly, Mondays 03:00 UTC, and `POST .../drift-check`, `ai.evaluate`): agreement over the last 7 days against the latest approved promotion's agreement; a drop beyond `maxAgreementDrop` with at least 20 compared cases sets `drift_fallback` (AI tasks of that version then run as `suggest`) and audits `ai.skill.drift-fallback`; `POST .../clear-drift` (`ai.approve-skill`, reason) clears it.
- Feedback: `POST /runs/{runId}/ai-decisions/{id}/outcome` (`accepted` or `overridden` with the final value and a reason; participants of the run, `run.operate` or `ai.evaluate`). Every override becomes a pending `ai_eval_candidate` (with values only when the decision retained them); `POST /ai-eval-candidates/{id}/review` accepts it into a suite with a redacted or synthetic input, or discards it. `GET /ai-review-queue` lists sampled automatic decisions nobody reviewed yet.
- Workspace AI policy (`GET/PUT /ai-policy`; update by `workspace.manage-access`, optimistic `expectedVersion`): `regulated`, `residency[]`, `inputRetention` (digest default, redactedValues, fullValues), `retentionDays` (365), `lowRiskLabels[]` (`skillKey:label`), `allowAutoWithReview`, classification actions; a regulated workspace never sends sensitive fields. The GET also lists the deployment's endpoints with their residency tags.

## 7. AI decision record (CG-A03)

`ai_decision_record`, one per AI task occurrence, written with the step completion: identity (run, step, occurrence, skill key, version and hash, autonomy and effective autonomy), model (profile, provider, model used, prompt hash), input (field names, SHA-256 digest of the mapped values; values only with `redactedValues` (the minimized values) or `fullValues`), output (label or fields, score, recommendation or summary, reasons, evidence spans by field and character offset, field confidence), raw and calibrated confidence, threshold, route, guardrails (minimization actions, samples, valid samples, agreement, repairs, schema enforced, calibration run, downgrades, deadline), unavailable reason, review sample flag, human outcome (who, value, reason, when), tokens, cost, latency and `retain_until`.

- Run detail: `GET /runs/{runId}/ai-decisions` (whoever may see the run; values only when retained and the viewer may see the request data) and the new "AI decisions" panel (accept or override for participants, operators and evaluators).
- Run evidence pack: section "AI decisions" with control facts only (skill and version, model, input digest, status, AI result, confidence, route, human outcome); no input values, extracted values or summaries, as the pack's payload policy requires.

## 8. Studio

- `aiTask` in the palette ("AI task"), canvas metadata, BPMN notation (service task with a route gateway), route texts, step outputs for the field picker, references kept when steps are renamed.
- `AiTaskInspector`: skill picker (approved version, evaluation gate and drift warnings), autonomy (only the levels the mode allows; above the promotion ceiling shows the compiler's reason), threshold, review sample, mapping of each skill input with per-input redaction, and a path editor with one slot per label and route.
- Mock mode: `src/mocks/aiSkills.ts` (one approved classify skill; no AI decisions on mock requests).

## Verification

- Compiler `AiTaskCompilerTest` (8): BPMN of an automatic classify task (triggerable task, route gateway, allowed expressions, manifest pin), approval/evaluation/promotion blockers and a designer pin, routes per mode and autonomy, input contract checks, answers absent on `aiUnavailable`, BPMN round trip (with and without a designer pin), shadow tasks without a gateway, simulator answers and routing. Full compiler suite: 891 tests before the shadow change, all passing.
- Application `ModelProvidersTest` (7, no Spring, WireMock): OpenAI-compatible (bearer, strict schema, no key for private endpoints), Anthropic (cache_control, output_config.format, version header, no temperature), Bedrock (SigV4 header, session token, forced answer tool, bearer API key), SigV4 test vector, Azure (deployment and api-version), Gemini API and Vertex (paths, auth, responseJsonSchema), failure classes without bodies.
- Application `AiTaskFlowTest` (3, real PostgreSQL and Flowable, AI answers from `AiTaskStub`): four-eyes approval (author refused, self-approval refused, approved versions immutable), the publish gate before and after a passing evaluation (metrics, recall, confusion, calibration), the manifest pin; shadow mode and the agreement dashboard, promotions one step at a time with a second approver, the regulated policy with a low-risk label, routing on `label:routine`, `needsReview` for the adverse label (`adverseRegulated`), `lowConfidence`, `aiUnavailable`, one repair; minimization (card number and e-mail never reach the provider), strict schema, the decision record (digest only), events, turn state and sealed input deleted at the end, overrides becoming candidates, the run evidence pack without values; residency refusing a US-only endpoint.
- Security matrix: the 27 new operations declare `x-orqix-permission` and `x-orqix-audit`; tSec01 calls them as foreign principals (404, no state change; the AI tables are in the snapshot).
- Frontend: `api:generate` + `api:check`, `tsc -b --noEmit`, ESLint clean; Vitest 206 files, 1422 tests (new `AiTaskInspector.test.tsx`, `AiDecisionsPanel.test.tsx`).
- Full backend `mvnw -o clean verify`: see the session report (run after this note was written).

## Not covered

- CG-A06 (document extraction over attachments, OCR providers, verification task) and CG-A07 (operator explain).
- Agents and `ToolChat` still use their own OpenRouter client; moving them onto `ProviderRegistry` (and holding agent conversations in the encrypted turn state) belongs to the agent-tools session. The SPI and `TurnVault` are ready for it.
- A Studio page for AI skills (authoring, approval, evaluation runs, shadow dashboard, promotions) and an AI review queue page: the API is complete, the UI shows skills only in the inspector and decisions only in run detail.
- Automatic human outcomes: the outcome is recorded explicitly; an approval that follows an AI task does not yet record it by itself.
- Prompt caching for OpenAI-compatible, Azure, Bedrock and Gemini endpoints beyond what those providers do automatically; streaming; log-probability calibration for providers other than OpenAI-compatible.
- Live provider accounts: every adapter is verified against the WireMock stand-in only.
- Retention purge of `ai_decision_record` past `retain_until` (the column is set; the purge job is not written).
